transcript:
Header: 2026-08-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Aurora Head of ML), Carlos Reyes (Aurora Platform), Priya Nair (Aurora Finance)

Summary: cost economics deep-dive, bench results review, plan next experiments for caching and batching.

[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on time, uh quick check — audio OK?
[00:08] Maya: Yep good here, thanks Sophie.
[00:12] Sophie: Cool, so agenda, uh quick recap of last week's run, show updated tokens per second per dollar model, discuss KV/prefix caching numbers Daniel pulled, then decide next steps and what aurora needs for finance sign-off.
[00:27] Daniel: I will share my screen in a sec, i pulled the bench logs, there are two variants: hosted rtx and dedicated a100-ish sim, not exact HW labels, some transcribe issues in the logs.
[00:36] Carlos: quick q — are we still using the 8k context model for most flows?
[00:40] Maya: yes majority 6-8k with long product descriptions, some customer chats shorter ~300 tokens.
[00:47] Daniel: ok good, so baseline numbers: hosted avg is ~1,200 tokens/sec per GPU at p95 under current batching, cost ~$0.045 per 1k tokens effective in our model. Dedicated sim gives ~2,400 tokens/sec on same work with quantized weights and continuous batching. There's variability though.
[01:10] Priya: can you translate tokens/sec/$ for finance — like how many 1M tokens per dollar?
[01:16] Sophie: yeah we did that in the spreadsheet, rough headline is hosted comes to ~22k tokens per dollar, dedicated with optimizations ~52k tokens per dollar, but that's heavily dependent on batching and cache hit rate.
[01:30] Maya: those are big diffs, what's driving it — is it quant, or batching, or the cache?
[01:35] Daniel: mostly batching + quantization; but KV/prefix cache adds more when you have repeated prefixes — for aurora product descriptions caching saved ~30% of token generation workload in the sim. Caveat: cache hit rate depends on traffic distribution.
[01:51] Carlos: we saw in our test traffic a lot of repeating prefixes for similar SKUs, so cache should help, but our burstiness is a concern.
[02:00] Sophie: right and batching helps in steady-state throughput but increases tail latency. We need to balance tokens/sec/$ vs latency SLO. What we recommended: adaptive batching with a per-route latency cap.
[02:14] Maya: can you show the spreadsheet numbers?
[02:16] Daniel: sure sharing now — link (redacted) https://redwood.app/sheets/aurora-cost-model (shared).
[02:22] [screen share noise] Daniel: So column A is traffic mix, B is average tokens per request, C is token/sec observed, D is cost per token, E derived tokens/sec per dollar. Row 12 is product desc flow where caching improves effective tokens/sec/$ from 40k to 58k at 45% cache hit.
[02:45] Priya: that 45% hit is optimistic — from finance we need worst case estimates too. Can you show a 10-20% hit scenario?
[02:53] Daniel: yes with 20% hit the effective tokens/sec/$ drops back to ~44k for that flow. We have a sensitivity table lower in the sheet.
[03:05] Maya: what about batching tradeoffs, at p99 latency — do we get big spikes?
[03:10] Daniel: p99 does increase; with batching target 32 requests per batch we saw p95 within SLO but p99 blips above. We can cap batching window to 50ms to control tail, which reduces peak tokens/sec by ~8-12% but keeps p99 acceptable.
[03:27] Carlos: any work on adaptive batching?
[03:29] Daniel: yes server runtime supports adaptive batching; we can set per-route warm-up thresholds. Works well with KV cache since cached prefixes short-circuit generation and reduce batch size.
[03:39] Sophie: also worth noting cold-start vs warm caches — first request after cache miss still pays full cost so we need to measure steady-state vs startup.
[03:47] Maya: do we have numbers for cold start cost across bursts?
[03:50] Daniel: I ran a burst sim — 5k concurrent requests, cache cold, tokens/sec/$ dropped to ~18k for duration of burst because GPUs saturate with full sequences; after 30-60s steady state resumes and cache hits climb.
[04:05] Priya: ok finance will assume a runway for bursts — we need a recommended fallback plan if we hit burst cost spike.
[04:11] Sophie: recommendation: enable region routing + burst capacity (reserved spare) or fallback to smaller model for degraded latency — both lower cost impact vs scaling full A100 pool. We'll send configs.
[04:23] Maya: what's the tradeoff when using smaller model — quality drop vs cost?
[04:26] Daniel: depends on prompt; for retrieval-augmented product description generation smaller 2B model can handle >90% cases but hallucination risk slightly up. We can A/B test.
[04:36] Carlos: can Redwood's runtime do automatic fallbacks?
[04:38] Sophie: yes we support routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants, and can set rollback policies. We'll show a sample rollout config.
[04:47] Maya: great. Also security/compliance note — audit logs and KMS were ok last week? Any blockers?
[04:52] Sophie: no blockers, we updated the SOC2 attestation in drive and KMS integration doc. Link: https://redwood.app/security/audit (shared).
[04:59] Priya: finance wants a one-pager for execs with clear token/sec/$ numbers and recommended pilot capacity and budget.
[05:05] Sophie: we'll produce that. Priya what's the budget window you are looking at?
[05:09] Priya: 3 month pilot with a $75k cap ideally. Need to see expected burn vs value.
[05:14] Sophie: we'll map that in the one-pager and show expected token throughput under different cache/batch mix scenarios.
[05:20] Maya: question on metrics — can we get per-route cost-per-100k requests in the console?
[05:24] Daniel: yes per-route token breakdown is available, and we can attach evals to detect quality regressions.
[05:28] Carlos: will you run the extra KV/prefix experiment we asked — measure hit rate when grouping by SKU family?
[05:33] Daniel: yes started that yesterday, will run larger sample and upload logs.
[05:36] Sophie: ok let's go through open items (quick).
[05:39] Sophie: item 1 — revised cost sheet link and headline tokens/sec/$ for hosted vs dedicated.
[05:44] Maya: item 2 — KV cache experiment for SKU families.
[05:47] Carlos: item 3 — anonymized traffic sample.
[05:49] Priya: item 4 — finance req for one-pager and pilot budget.
[05:52] Sophie: any blockers on your side?
[05:54] Maya: we'll be able to provide traffic sample by end of week, trying to sanitize PII.
[05:58] Carlos: platform side ok to run the traces.
[06:01] Priya: i need the one-pager by monday next week.
[06:04] Sophie: we'll aim for friday to give you breathing room.
[06:07] [brief pause]
[06:10] Daniel: technical note — prefix caching needs careful invalidation when product descriptions change; we recommend TTL + versioned cache keys. Implementation is straightforward in runtime.
[06:23] Maya: good to know.
[06:25] Sophie: last thing — can we commit to a short benchmark next Tue where Redwood runs a dedicated sim on your traffic sample and we present numbers?
[06:33] Maya: yes Tue works.
[06:35] Sophie: perfect. Quick recap and next steps — we'll send revised spreadsheet, one-pager, rollout config, and Daniel's KV logs. Action items recorded. Thanks everyone.
[06:47] Priya: thanks all.
[06:49] Maya: thanks.
[06:50] Sophie: bye.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings and shorthand, as typical of Fireflies exports. Links in conversation point to shared Redwood docs/drive.
